notes: kb/Work PB5677 (2026-11-17): GR4b3's 'data is moved as if the sending operand were described as an unsigned numeric integer' is built for a figurative constant whose character is a digit, which a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE makes of LOW-VALUE or HIGH-VALUE: with ALPHABET ALF5 IS "5", MOVE LOW-VALUE TO PIC 9(3)V99 stored 555.55 (the image 55555) and to PIC ZZ9.99 the image 555555; the string of as many 5s as the item has character positions (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3) is an integer aligned by decimal point, so the items hold 555.00 and 555.00. MoveEmitter.AllLiteralNumber, the one decider of the number a fill sends, now answers for such a figurative at 85 as it did for a digit-only ALL literal; a fill of a character that is no digit keeps the image fill (its value the implementor's). The witness pb5677_figurative_digit_to_noninteger_85 runs it into 9(3)V99, ZZ9.99, $$9.99, S9(3)V99 SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE, 9(3), COMP-3 and COMP, beside the nonnumeric literal of the same characters. || kb/Work PB5852 (2026-11-16): GR4b1's 'the sign of the sending operand is placed in the receiving item' is built for a sender truncated to zero: MOVE -100 TO S99 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE stores -00 (it stored +00, the PARTIAL of the 1985 code reads, batch 10 mechanism 13, kb/Work/PB5683/2026-11-16-rulings-code-reads-batch-10.md). An image-carried signed DISPLAY receiver is written by CobolNum.FormatImageSendersSign with the sender read once and its sign taken from that one read (MoveEmitter.SendersSign), and StorageFormPass promotes to its image each native signed DISPLAY receiver a store can hand a negative zero (SendersSignStore.MayHandNegativeZero, a computed set closed over the stores; DESIGN-data-model §2.1.1); DialectBehavior.MoveSignIsTheValuesSign ends the arm at 2014 (VCR row 7.85). A literal is its value, "the algebraic quantity represented by the characters in the numeric literal" (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.2 GR4), and the value zero has no sign to place, so MOVE -0 stores a positive zero (the witness line LIT-0 gives +00). The witness pb5852_move_sign_of_sending_operand runs the five lines of the note, a negative zero moved on, low-order truncation, INITIALIZE, a file round trip, an unsigned receiver, a positive sender and the -0 literal. The account that follows is the stored CONFORMS account of the rest of the rule. || §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4: 'Any necessary conversion of data from one form of internal representation to another takes place during legal elementary moves', with a) alignment/space fill and no sign or de-editing into alphanumeric receivers, b) decimal-point alignment, de-editing, sign rules 1-2 and 3) an alphanumeric sender (GR3: 'All other figurative constants belong to the category alphanumeric') 'moved as if the sending operand were described as an unsigned numeric integer', c) alphabetic justification. One emitter serves every edition: MoveEmitter.ElementaryStore dispatches on MoveClassifier.Kind to ConvertSource (CharacterStore/SendingCharacters for character receivers; NumericRenderer.AlnumNum/CobolNum.FromAlphanumericSending and CobolEdit.DeEdit for numeric ones) or FigurativeToNumericImageStore. The prior PARTIAL's three faults are gone at --std 85: digit-only ALL into 999V99 gives 555.00 (as the PIC X(5) item does), into ZZ9.99 is edited (555.00), and QUOTE/HIGH-VALUE/ALL "AB" into COMP and COMP-3 run (undefined value, no abort). Also probed: signed, trailing/leading separate, P-scaled senders into X and JUSTIFIED X, alphanumeric-edited (and onto itself), alphabetic truncate/fill, signed into unsigned, COMP into COMP-3, CR and $ edited senders de-edited into signed/unsigned/edited, 18-digit negative, ALL "12"/ALL "123" into noninteger, ZERO into edited and X. The witness runs three of these moves.
